agree.reason: Starting with traffic, admitting the morning backups, and asking for the signal as a binding condition gives the two traffic-focused commissioners an easy yes; skeptical neighbours get less, because the speech leaves out the written offer of weekday parking and the promised neighbour group.

honest.reason: The figures are accurate and the speaker admits that traffic matters, but 'busiest intersection' is invented and 'exactly the families who are waiting' assumes the waiting-list households qualify, which the facts don't establish.

works_the_facts.reason: Apart from '72 spaces is more than one per unit', the speech only repeats numbers; it never works out, for example, how much of the 412-household waiting list these 64 homes would house (about one in six).

right_comparison.reason: It sets C-with-signal against D-without and an unused lot against a three-year wait, but it never spells out the do-nothing outcome: the lot stays empty and the waiting list stays where it is.

qualification.reason: 'As long as the signal actually gets built' is a real, checkable condition tied to approval, but it gives no deadline (for example, before occupancy) and no consequence if the signal is never built.

objections.reason: Traffic and parking are answered, but the 20 months of construction trucks on Alder Road go unmentioned, and so do the strongest replies to neighbours: the written weekday-parking offer and the speaker's own seat on the neighbour group.

fit.reason: At roughly 400 words it fits a three-minute spoken slot and reads naturally aloud, though it leaves '[your name]' as a placeholder.
